headline: Morbi normalises in Q2, but a rise again in propane prices could drive volumes

highlights: Morbi volumes moderated to ~3.9mmscmd (vs. ~5.6mmscmd in Q1) as propane availability improved and prices of propane fell in Q2.
Trading EBITDA rose 91% YoY to INR 3.3bn, but Q2 trading margin was ~4% (Qatar force majeure); H2 guidance of 5–6% is intact.
Valuations of 6.1x FY28E PER/4.2x EV/EBITDA are attractive; TP is retained at INR 345.
Volume uptick in non-Morbi industrial and domestic/CNG, and an easing of LNG costs could aid GEL’s long-term prospects.
valuation: Valuations of 6.1x FY28E PER/4.2x EV/EBITDA are attractive; TP is retained at INR 345.
GEL added 18 CNG stations in H1 (total 857) and targets 75+ in FY27, with double- digit CNG growth as the goal.
Valuations are unchallenging at ~6.1x FY28E EPS and 4.2x EV/EBITDA.
watch: With strong growth in domestic/CNG segment, steady improvement in I/C volumes from areas other than Morbi and synergies in gas sourcing/tax benefits and efficiencies post the GSPC merger, we see risk-reward as favourable at current prices (stock has fallen 39% in last 12M).
Key upside risks: 1) Sharper recovery in LPG (propane) prices; 2) faster execution of expansion plans in new areas; and 3) sharp drop in LNG prices.
